threads.title: Fulfill as prophecy bringing to pass
threads.summary_md: The Greek *plēroō* (Strong's G4137) at Matthew 5:17 does not mean *to exhaust-and-thereby-end* — the antichrist reading the pulpit installed to retire the Torah. It means *to bring to pass* — to make happen what was prophesied. Yahusha (Jesus) names what his mission accomplishes: the bringing-to-pass of what the Torah and the Prophets prophesied. And what they prophesied is the gathering of the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) home through redemption — the curse-and-return arc the Torah itself wrote (Leviticus 26:33 and 40-42; Deuteronomy 30:1-5), executed by the prophets in the divorce-and-scattering (Hosea 1:9; Jeremiah 16:13), and opened by the Messiah's death and resurrection so the door home is real. This thread surfaces every NT plēroō occurrence used in prophecy-fulfillment context (35 members), each linked to the specific Tanakh prophecy it brings to pass. The pattern is consistent: the Messiah walks out the substance the prophets foretold, and the NT formula *that it might be fulfilled* points the reader back to the Tanakh, not forward into a new dispensation.

Soldiers casting lots fulfills Psalm 22:18 — *they part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.* Psalm 22 in its entirety is the crucifixion-foretelling psalm; v.18 is the specific cross-scene predictor.

threads.title: The kings and the mighty condemning the Elect One, and the Elect One vindicated on the throne of his glory — 1 Enoch 62-63 beside Matthew 27
threads.summary_md: *When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Yahusha (Jesus) to put him to death:* (Matthew 27:1). David had seen that council: *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,* (Psalm 2:2). By the afternoon the same men are under the cross: *He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:42-43). Enoch saw the other end of that scene. He saw the day the kings and the mighty are summoned to look at the one they condemned: *And thus Yahuah (Lord) commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted, and those who dwell on the earth, and said: 'Open your eyes and lift up your horns if ye are able to recognize the Elect One.'* (1 Enoch 62:1); *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). He could have called twelve legions of angels at Gethsemane and did not, because the one who was hidden from the beginning was walking the road the Father laid for him: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). His cry from the cross is the opening line of Psalm 22, and that psalm does not end forsaken; it ends with the Father hearing and all the ends of the earth turning to him. The Father did not abandon the Son; the Son prayed the psalm the way the Suffering Servant was always going to pray it, through to its end. And the men who mocked will one day beg for a moment's respite: *In those days shall the mighty and the kings who possess the earth implore (Him) to grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment to whom they were delivered, that they might fall down and worship before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, and confess their sins before Him.* (1 Enoch 63:1), and they will say what they refused to say at Golgotha: *And splendid in every secret thing is Thy power from generation to generation, And Thy glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Thy secrets and innumerable, And Thy righteousness is beyond reckoning.* (1 Enoch 63:3). Paul says every knee will bow at the name of Yahusha, things in heaven, in earth and under the earth. The cross and the throne are the same figure seen from two days.

members_in_this_chapter.member_note: *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). *When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Yahusha (Jesus) to put him to death* (Matthew 27:1). Enoch saw the other morning: all the kings and the mighty standing up in that day to see and recognize how he sits on the throne of his glory, where no lying word is spoken. The council that condemned him stands at his bar.

*And He will summon all the host of the heavens, and all the holy ones above, and the host of Elohim (God), the Cherubin, Seraphin and Ophannin, and all the angels of power, and all the angels of principalities, and the Elect One, and the other powers on the earth (and) over the water.* (1 Enoch 61:10). *If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him* (Matthew 27:42). The mockers set the wrong test. Enoch saw the King's credential: the whole host of heaven summoned, and the Elect One among them. He did not come down from the cross; he is the one for whom the heavens are mustered.

*And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14). *He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him* (Matthew 27:43). The Head of Days had already said it: *the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.* The cross was not the Father's forsaking of the Son; it was the Son of Adam, born unto righteousness, doing what righteousness does.

*And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). *Let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him* (Matthew 27:42). Enoch saw the mockers' end: the kings and the mighty and those who rule the earth falling on their faces before that Son of Adam, worshipping and petitioning. *Every knee should bow* (Philippians 2:10) — the mockers included.
